title: On which day were the fewest library books borrowed?
description: A chart with one open book for each book shows the books borrowed on each day of a week. Reading it gives the quietest day, the total for the week and the busiest day with a likely reason.
teaching_notes: One idea: an empty row means zero, so it is the smallest, and the total is the sum of all the rows. Watch for children who skip the empty row or leave a row out of the sum.

source: Figure it Out: books borrowed in a week from the library of Middle School, Ginnori
video_script.why: The child reads a chart with one symbol for one book, treats an empty row as zero, and adds every row for the total.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own library chart
video_script.anchor: the library chart of a middle school in Ginnori, with a row of open books for each day
video_script.payoff_line: The fewest books were borrowed on Thursday, and twenty four books were borrowed in all.

final_answer.value: a Thursday; b 24; c Saturday (Sunday is a holiday, so students can read the borrowed books on Sunday)
final_answer.spoken: the fewest books on Thursday, twenty four books in all, and the most books on Saturday, because Sunday is a holiday

never_show: the busiest day and its reason before the last steps
maths_rules: Monday 5, Tuesday 4, Wednesday 2, Thursday 0 (empty row), Friday 5, Saturday 8.
The smallest count is 0 on Thursday and the largest is 8 on Saturday.
video_script.design: Six rows of open books, one for each day from Monday to Saturday, with Thursday an empty row.

beats.on_screen: title card with a school library shelf and a chart of six rows of open books, one row for each day

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the library and the chart
marks.week: the six day rows light up from Monday to Saturday
marks.ask: a question mark lights up beside the chart

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a school library in Ginnori.
<bookmark mark='week'/>A chart shows the books that students borrowed on each day of a week.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On which days were the fewest and the most books borrowed?

beats.on_screen: the chart and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one open book beside the words one book, and an empty row beside the words nothing borrowed

marks.book: the key one open book equals one book is circled
marks.empty: an empty row appears with a zero beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>In this chart, one open book stands for one book that was borrowed.
<bookmark mark='empty'/>A row with no open book means that no book was borrowed.

beats.on_screen: Given: key 1 open book = 1 book; one row for each day, Monday to Saturday

marks.given: the key and the six day rows are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a chart with one row for each day from Monday to Saturday.

beats.on_screen: To find: a. the day with the fewest books, b. the total for the week, c. the day with the most books and a possible reason

marks.find: the three lines to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the fewest, the total, and the most, with a reason.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: count the open books in each row: Monday 5, Tuesday 4, Wednesday 2, Thursday 0, Friday 5, Saturday 8

marks.first: the books of Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday are counted and the numbers written
marks.empty: the empty row of Thursday gets a zero
marks.last: the books of Friday and Saturday are counted and the numbers written

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, count the open books in each row. Monday has five, Tuesday has four, and Wednesday has two.
<bookmark mark='empty'/>Thursday has an empty row, which means zero.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Friday has five, and Saturday has eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the smallest count is 0, in the empty row

marks.smallest: the zero in the empty row is circled and set beside the smallest other count, 2

narration: <bookmark mark='smallest'/>Step two, find the smallest count.
Zero is smaller than two, so the empty row has the fewest books.

marks.add: the six counts are added in a line, with the zero kept in the sum

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the counts of the whole week.
Five, four, two, zero, five and eight make twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: the largest count is 8, on Saturday; Sunday is a holiday, so students can read the books on Sunday

marks.largest: the row of eight books is circled
marks.reason: a Sunday card with a holiday sign and a child reading appears

narration: <bookmark mark='largest'/>Step four, find the largest count. Eight is larger than all the others.
<bookmark mark='reason'/>Sunday is a holiday, so students can read the borrowed books on Sunday.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. Thursday; b. 24 books; c. Saturday, because Sunday is a holiday and students can read the books on Sunday

marks.ans: the first two answers are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The fewest books were borrowed on Thursday, and twenty four books were borrowed in all.
<bookmark mark='most'/>The most books were borrowed on Saturday, because Sunday is a holiday for reading.
